newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil gains on futures, some see slump over.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil gains on futures, some see slump over.

text.p: NWE gas oil strengthened on Wednesday on the back of firmer IPE futures.
March IPE gas oil was trading $2.25 higher at $166.00 at 1300 GMT.

Traders said there was a lot of talk in the market that gas oil had bottomed out after recent heavy losses. Front month gas oil has fallen almost non-stop since the end of January from around $212 a tonne to about $166 today.
"There is a feeling that the market found its bottom last week," said one trader who said he had seen a slight improvement in activity.
Others felt that if German demand rose and interest generally improved over the next couple of days then the recovery might be sustainable.
"The next couple of days will be crucial," said one.

Bears cited no change in the fundamental supply/demand scenario and claimed the recent rise was technically driven. Bulls pointed to the weakness of gas oil relative to crude saying a current spread of around $17 a tonne compares with about $33 a tonne this time last year.
But, European weather remains mild and temperatures in the northeastern U.S give little support.
